title: Contrast preservation and brand-state tokens for dense data components
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Brand accent colors provided by customers and partners are highly variable and sometimes break contrast when applied to compact UI surfaces (table rows, compact buttons, sparkline overlays). Goal: define a deterministic token-mapping and override strategy that preserves WCAG contrast targets for interactive surfaces and ensures readable data visualizations in dark mode while maintaining brand accents where possible. This ticket covers the design proposals, example token mappings, accessibility thresholds, and a set of component-level overrides for tables, buttons, and small charts.
acceptance_criteria: A design token mapping table exists that maps generic brand accent inputs to safe-on-surface values for both light and dark themes
Buttons (primary, ghost, destructive) meet 4.5:1 contrast for text/icons on all supported densities when brand accents are applied
Table row states (hover, selected, flagged) have distinct accessible colors and maintain row striping where applicable
Compact charts and sparklines use adapted brand accents or generated palettes that maintain visual separability and 3:1 contrast for data items against background
A small set of component overrides (CSS token names + usage guidance) is documented for engineering and included in the design tokens package PR
engineering_notes: ENG will implement a server-side token sanitizer that converts submitted brand hex values through the mapping table before emitting runtime tokens
We recommend exposing two generated tokens for each brand accent: --brand-accent-safe (guaranteed contrast) and --brand-accent-raw (useful for decorative non-interactive backgrounds)
A fallback algorithm for out-of-gamut colors: desaturate by 20% then mix with surface color at 30% to raise contrast. This is proposed rather than clamp to black/white to preserve hue.
KV cache of computed safe tokens should be keyed by brand id + theme mode to avoid recomputation on every render
comments: 2026-02-16 - Asha Patel: Initial discovery complete. Collected 24 customer brand palettes from onboarding and noted 6 palettes that fail contrast on compact buttons in dark mode.

2026-02-20 - Liam Chen: Prototyped mapping algorithm in Figma using color-mix approach (desaturate + mix with surface). Early results look promising for maintaining hue while hitting contrast targets.

2026-02-25 - Priya Nair (PM): Asked for a fallback policy for 'critical' interactive elements where 4.5:1 must be strictly enforced even if brand is lost. Suggested the pragmatic approach of preserving brand on decorative elements only.

2026-03-02 - Accessibility review (external): Recommended 4.5:1 for text and 3:1 for large icons; flagged tight-coupled small chart color separability as a special case where explicit palette generation is required.
2026-03-05 - Design Review: Decided to add two new semantic tokens: semantic-state-accent and semantic-data-accent to separate interactive state accents from chart/palette accents.
2026-03-08 - Engineering feedback: ENG-7712 can provide a theming middleware hook; will need token names and usage examples before dev work starts.
2026-03-10 - Liam Chen: Draft of token mapping table posted to Confluence; ready for final design sign-off and handoff to ENG
decision_log: Do not allow raw brand hex to be applied directly to interactive text/buttons in dark mode; require mapping to a safe token
Introduce semantic tokens to separate interactive accents from decorative/data accents
Prefer hue-preserving desaturation+mix fallback over pure luminance clamping to retain brand character
Provide two levels of fallback: conservative (for critical elements) and permissive (for decorative/data elements)
